check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 warnings).

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 47 stocks
   line 40:  p20.aspirate(5, src_well)
   At line 40 the tip went into library 9 (well A2 in slot 1), library 17 (well A3 in slot
   1), library 25 (well A4 in slot 1), library 33 (well A5 in slot 1) and 43 more while it
   still carried library 1 (well A1 in slot 1), library 9 (well A2 in slot 1), library 17
   (well A3 in slot 1), library 25 (well A4 in slot 1) and 43 more from an earlier step
   (this line did it 47 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in
   the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there.
   The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left
   in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 39 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 40 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [bb98fed9822b]

2. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: Tube A1 in slot 2 never mixed after library 48 went in (2% of the
well)
   line 41:  p20.dispense(5, pool_tube)
   At line 41 the robot added library 48 to tube A1 in slot 2, which already held library 1,
   library 2, library 3, library 4 and 43 more. The addition was 2% of the well, nothing
   mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with it that way. Two liquids layered in a
   small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration
   you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will
   mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix tube A1 in slot 2 after line 41: `mix_after=(5, 192)` on the transfer, or
   `pipette.mix(5, 192, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [339828025b70]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
